findings.source_passage: The abnormal mind is quick to detect and attach itself to this quality when it appears in a normal person, and so it came about that in college I was unjustly accused of being a politician
findings.source_locator: Opening paragraph, after 'victim of not a few veteran bores'
findings.why_it_matters: This passage is both voice-establishing and interpretively weighted — it defines Nick's self-conception as a reluctant confessor and frames his entire narrative stance. The deleted material includes the distinctive phrase about 'intimate revelations of young men' being 'plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions,' which is signature Fitzgerald irony and critical-tradition territory.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full passage from 'The abnormal mind is quick to detect' through 'plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions' before the 'Reserving judgements is a matter of infinite hope' sentence, which the draft correctly preserves.

findings.source_passage: This responsiveness had nothing to do with that flabby impressionability which is dignified under the name of the 'creative temperament'—it was an extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness
findings.source_locator: Third paragraph of the novel, the Gatsby characterization block
findings.why_it_matters: The contrast between 'flabby impressionability' and 'extraordinary gift for hope' is a critically celebrated distinction that defines Gatsby's nature and Nick's moral framework for the entire novel. The draft jumps directly to 'It was an extraordinary gift for hope,' losing the rhetorical opposition and the 'creative temperament' phrase that critics consistently engage with.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence beginning 'This responsiveness had nothing to do with that flabby impressionability...' before the preserved 'It was an extraordinary gift for hope' clause.

findings.source_passage: Conduct may be founded on the hard rock or the wet marshes, but after a certain point I don't care what it's founded on.
findings.source_locator: Fourth paragraph, before 'When I came back from the East'
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is one of the most quoted lines in the novel's opening, establishing Nick's moral exhaustion and relativism; its Biblical resonance and rhetorical compactness make it a signature line that critics and readers alike return to.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the sentence 'Conduct may be founded on the hard rock or the wet marshes, but after a certain point I don't care what it's founded on.' immediately before the 'When I came back from the East' sentence.

findings.source_passage: The lawn started at the beach and ran towards the front door for a quarter of a mile, jumping over sundials and brick walks and burning gardens—finally when it reached the house drifting up the side in bright vines as though from the momentum of its run.
findings.source_locator: Description of the Buchanan house exterior, before Tom on the front porch
findings.why_it_matters: This is a prosodically distinctive, much-admired sentence — the personification of the lawn 'jumping' and then 'drifting' is a signature stylistic moment that establishes the dreamy grandeur of East Egg and Fitzgerald's lyrical method. Its absence flattens the arrival scene.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full lawn sentence before or after the brief mention of the Buchanan house being a 'cheerful red-and-white Georgian Colonial mansion.'

findings.source_passage: a gruff husky tenor, added to the impression of fractiousness he conveyed. There was a touch of paternal contempt in it, even toward people he liked—and there were men at New Haven who had hated his guts.
findings.source_locator: Tom's physical description, after 'a cruel body'
findings.why_it_matters: Tom's voice characterization — the 'paternal contempt' and the men at New Haven who 'hated his guts' — is central to establishing his menace and social violence. It is interpretively loaded and feeds directly into readings of Tom's class aggression throughout the novel.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two sentences about Tom's voice and the 'paternal contempt' after the 'cruel body' sentence that the draft preserves.

findings.source_passage: I looked back at my cousin, who began to ask me questions in her low, thrilling voice. It was the kind of voice that the ear follows up and down, as if each speech is an arrangement of notes that will never be played again.
findings.source_locator: After Jordan Baker's introduction, Daisy's voice description
findings.why_it_matters: The draft preserves a shortened echo ('the kind the ear follows up and down') but strips the full sentence shape and loses the crucial second clause — 'an arrangement of notes that will never be played again' — which is one of the novel's most quoted characterizations of Daisy and becomes a motif when Gatsby later identifies her voice as 'full of money.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the complete sentence: 'It was the kind of voice that the ear follows up and down, as if each speech is an arrangement of notes that will never be played again.'

findings.source_passage: Something was making him nibble at the edge of stale ideas as if his sturdy physical egotism no longer nourished his peremptory heart.
findings.source_locator: Final paragraph of the dinner scene, before 'Already it was deep summer'
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is the interpretive key to Tom's psychological state — his white-supremacist reading and his affair are both symptoms of the same spiritual vacancy. Critics rely on this exact phrasing. The draft preserves the surrounding sentence about Tom being 'depressed by a book' but drops this crucial analytical follow-through.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sentence 'Something was making him nibble at the edge of stale ideas as if his sturdy physical egotism no longer nourished his peremptory heart.' after the observation about Tom being depressed by a book.

findings.source_passage: I felt that Tom would drift on forever seeking, a little wistfully, for the dramatic turbulence of some irrecoverable football game.
findings.source_locator: Paragraph about why the Buchanans came East, after 'I didn't believe it'
findings.why_it_matters: This is a signature characterization of Tom — the football game as the peak of his existence — and is one of the novel's most cited psychological portraits. The draft omits the entire paragraph about the Buchanans drifting from polo ground to polo ground, erasing an important ironic register passage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the paragraph beginning 'Why they came East I don't know' including the 'irrecoverable football game' clause, which crystallizes Tom's stunted character in a way the novel returns to.

summary: The draft drops three high-severity signature passages from the novel's famous opening (the 'hard rock or wet marshes' line, the 'flabby impressionability'/'creative temperament' contrast, and the 'abnormal mind'/'plagiaristic revelations' voice block) plus five medium-severity losses including Daisy's full voice description, Tom's 'peremptory heart' sentence, the football-game characterization, Tom's 'paternal contempt' voice portrait, and the Buchanan lawn's signature kinetic sentence — collectively requiring regeneration.
